package_metadata.name: napari-mlarray
package_metadata.summary: napari reader and writer for MLArray (.mla) images, with correct physical geometry and orientation.
package_metadata.description:
# napari-mlarray

A [napari](https://napari.org) reader and writer for [MLArray](https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/mlarray) (`.mla`) files that shows every image where it physically is, in the orientation radiologists expect. ```bash pip install napari-mlarray # into an existing napari installation pip install "napari-mlarray[all]" # with napari and Qt ``` Drag a `.mla` file into napari, or `File > Open`. To convert NIfTI, NRRD, MetaImage, MGH or DICOM to `.mla`, use [MedVol](https://mic-dkfz.github.io/MedVol/): `medvol convert ct.nii.gz ct.mla`. ## What you see napari knows nothing about patient anatomy: a layer is an array plus an affine into "world" coordinates, and the 2-D canvas shows the last two world dims (down and right). napari-mlarray chooses the world so that the default camera gives the familiar picture, with no flips or rotations to fix by hand: | plane (`viewer.dims.order`) | screen up | screen right | |---|---|---| | axial `(0, 1, 2)` | anterior | patient left (radiological) | | coronal `(1, 0, 2)` | superior | patient left (radiological) | | sagittal `(2, 0, 1)` | superior | posterior | - The world axes of a patient image point to **I, P, L** (labelled in napari's dims slider). This frame is right-handed, so the 3-D view is not mirrored. With the `neurological` convention they point to **I, P, R** (patient left on the screen's left) and the plugin flips the 3-D camera depth to keep 3-D unmirrored. - Every voxel is placed exactly from the file's geometry (`spaces[0]`): any storage order (axial, sagittal, coronal, flipped) gives the same picture, and images of different grids overlay correctly. The array is reordered for display only, never resampled, unless the grid is oblique (below). - World coordinates are millimetres. Convert the cursor position back to the file's patient coordinates (DICOM LPS) with `napari_mlarray.letters_to_lps(viewer.dims.axis_labels[-3:]).T @ viewer.cursor.position[-3:]`. This is verified on screen by [`scripts/verify_orientation.py`](scripts/verify_orientation.py) (napari 0.10): a letter phantom stored axially, RAS-flipped, sagittally and obliquely gives the same, correct picture in all three planes and an unmirrored 3-D view, in both conventions. Other spaces work the same way: earth-observation spaces are shown north up and east right, spaces without direction words in reversed axis order (`z, y, x`), so an identity matrix shows the array as NumPy does. ### Oblique images napari cannot slice an affine that rotates the displayed axes against the slicing axis in 2-D (it drops the out-of-plane rotation). For grids that are oblique to the world axes, choose: | `oblique` | effect | |---|---| | `resample` (default) | resampled onto a world-aligned grid (linear for images, nearest neighbour for labels): exact positions | | `nearest` | axes snapped to the closest world axes, as ITK-SNAP and MRIcroGL do: upright, but positions are approximate | | `keep` | the exact affine: correct in 3-D, approximate in 2-D slices | ### Settings ```python import napari_mlarray napari_mlarray.set_display(convention="neurological", oblique="nearest") # for files opened from now on layers = napari_mlarray.add_mlarray(viewer, "ct.mla", convention="radiological") # one file, explicit options ``` or set `NAPARI_MLARRAY_CONVENTION` / `NAPARI_MLARRAY_OBLIQUE` before starting napari. ## Layers | content of the file | napari layer | |---|---| | `values.kind` `measurement` (and others) | Image; `values.scale`/`offset` applied (e.g. Hounsfield units), contrast limits from `ml` statistics when present | | `values.kind` `label` or `instance` | Labels, with names, colours and codes of `values.labels` (shown when hovering) | | a `channel` axis | one Image layer per channel, named after the axis labels (`ct [T1]`, `ct [T2]`, ...) | | `time` and other axes | sliders; time is in its unit (`start`, `step`) | | a 2-D grid in a 3-D space (a single DICOM slice) | a one-slice volume at its position, so it overlays with volumes | | `profiles.ml.boxes` (3-D) | Labels layer of box outlines: every slice in every plane shows the box, and so does 3-D; hovering shows label and score | | `profiles.ml.boxes` (2-D) | Shapes rectangles with label and score | Boxes are drawn by [napari-bboxes](https://github.com/Karol-G/napari-bboxes), which you can also use on its own for boxes from any source. Files larger than 1 GiB are read slice by slice and stay on disk. Labels are always loaded, so you can paint. ## Saving `File > Save Selected Layer(s)` with a `.mla` name writes Image and Labels layers: - A layer opened from a `.mla` file is written in its original array order with all its metadata: axes, values and label table, profiles, user metadata, source headers and history (plus an `edited` entry). Value scaling applied for display is undone when that is exact. The geometry comes from the layer's current transform, so a layer you moved is saved where it is shown. - A new layer (for example labels you painted on an image) is written in the patient frame (LPS) when the viewer shows patient axes (`I, P, L` or `I, P, R`), so it lines up with the image in any other tool. Label names from the layer's features (`index`, `name`) become the label table. ## Development ```bash pip install -e . --group dev pytest ``` The tests check every voxel's world position for axial, sagittal, flipped and RAS-stored grids in both conventions, oblique grids, labels, channels, time, single slices, boxes and save/load round trips. `xvfb-run python scripts/verify_orientation.py OUTDIR` checks the picture on screen. ## License Distributed under the terms of the MIT license. ## Acknowledgments
